Elk Hunting is a major activity in the West. There are two main species of Elk or Wapiti as the native Americans called them. There is the Roosevelt Elk which perfers the rainy coastal ranges and the Rocky Mountain Elk which likes the higher and dryer elevations.Buy the way the American Wapiti has been transplanted into New Zealand of all places. I hear they are doing rather well in the southern climes, I am lead to believe that the Elk has been successfully cross bred with native species and both the pure bred and the cross bred are commercially farmed in New Zealand.

Now back to the Hunting of the Wapiti. First of all the Rocky Mountain Elk is a big animal. Bulls can weigh in at 1200 lbs while Cow will go about 900. (That is bigger that the steers sold for slaughter in the United states). Secondly the Bull Elk is a tough animal to put down humanely. The Elk is is a wary animal that can run like the wind up hill through thick brush. I know a lot of guys that use .270's, 7mm mags, 308 Winchesters and .30/06's to take Elk. They are successful too, but what they don't tell you is how many animals the wound and that get away. The Elk is just too tough to take down at longer ranges with the intermediate calibers. I personally skinned out a medium size bull that took a heavy loaded (2500 fps) 220 grain projectile out of a .30/06 at 50 yards. The bullet was still lodged in chest cavity after piercing the lungs and heart. I that Bull would have been 200 yards it would have been a wounded animal that got away. That goes to show you how tough a Elk is. I don't recommend that you go after Elk with anything smaller than a .300 Magnum. The .338 Winchester Mag is ideal. I use my .375 H&H exclusively on Elk.

Now on to this antler point business. A one to two year bull is generally called a spike bull as they only have the main antler beams. The next up is a 2 two a 3 year bull (in good habitat) and they generally have large 5 point rack. The next year they get a rather small 6 point rack. After the 5 year almost all bulls will be a 6X6 point rack. The older they get the hat racks don't generally add more points they just get heavier, taller and wider.l

I suspect that the antlers of an Elk grow to size rather quickly because of breeding pressure on young bulls. If you are going to fight for a fair maiden you got to have the artillery.

(Side story here and its not about Elk) I was Elk hunting in the Wenaha Tucannon wilderness area in Oregon, (66,375 acres) and ran across a band of Rocky Mountain Big Horn Sheep. What was going on were two RAMs were fighting for breading rights to about 6 Ewes. The RAMS had between a half and a 3/4 curl to the Antlers. Well these to guys were battling it out with charge after charge. Then along comes the little RAM with less than a quarter curl. What does he do. Well He rounds up the Ewes and herds them up over the ridge and runs away with them. (The Moral here is MAKE LOVE NOT WAR)
